findings.expected: Where the push is past what the ground bears, the ground gets at most what it can bear, as real physics says for a yielding ground (roughly the bearing force over the push, or the push the real ground allows). The rest comes from their power (the endless ocean, the stated momentum exception). The shaking, the plaster and feel reaches and the ceilings should follow from that. If the author reads the canon differently, it needs the owners' ruling, recorded as a decision and in STATUS 'Waiting on'.
findings.fix: In each toGround or pushOff on unbreakable ground, cap J at the real ground's impulse: min(J, (bearing force + weight) × T), or the push from the same move on real ground. Report the rest as supplied by their power, and change the page wording ('that push still goes into the ground') to match. verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. CLAUDE.md canon says: 'Where the ground couldn't bear the push, their power supplies it (an exception to the momentum rule).' The brief's Why paragraph says the same, and STATUS records that the owner agreed to both momentum exceptions. The page's own assumptions card repeats it ('their power supplies it (a canon exception)'). jumpOnce does the opposite. With ctx.unbreakable it sets pushOff = { J: p, T: push.t }, which is all of his momentum, whatever the real ground could bear. MOVES.jump.shake turns that into ground shaking. If the ground takes all the momentum there is no exception, so the engine contradicts the canon and the page's own card. Physically, ground that gives at its bearing passes on at most about the bearing force over the push. With the full push, the shaking is overstated many times over on soil, and on concrete or asphalt at high dials (F/RBreal = 4.2 at 10^6 kg). That sets the Jump tab's courtesy ceiling and presets: sand at 10^6 kg shows a 4.5% ceiling set by plaster cracking at 5 m. None of the 21 recorded decisions covers this, and neither STATUS 'Waiting on' nor the README raises it. A throw, shove or catch with They take their own recoil on is covered by 5d (the planet keeps the momentum), so for those the full push is correct. The affected cases are the jump push-off, which 5d excludes, and Unbreakable-footing-only pushes with recoil off.
